newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close modestly lower in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close modestly lower in heavy trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed easier on Tuesday on heavy volume after profit-taking outweighed index futures-linked buying which had pushed the Hang Seng Index to a record high of 14,618.36 in early trade, brokers said.
The blue-chip index fell 34.48 points, or 0.24 percent, to finish at 14,540.16, off the low of 14,505.94.
Turnover was the third highest ever at HK$17.92 billion against the record of HK$20.59 billion set on Monday.
"Players are cautious at this high level and used the HKMA's remarks on Monday to take profits on properties," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Monday additional restraints in home mortgage lending might be needed as growth in lending had resulted in an increase in banks' property exposure.
Cheung Kong eased HK$1.00 to HK$79.00, Henderson Land fell HK$2.25 to HK$75.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$0.75 to HK$95.50.
Howard Gorges, vice chairman of South China Holdings, said the market was dominated by Hongkong Telecom and red chips while most blue chips were taking a breather.
"From the index there is nothing to talk about...except that Hongkong Telecom is up strongly," Gorges said.
Hongkong Telecom shares rose HK$0.65 to HK$16.80, just a touch off from the year high of HK$16.85 they hit earlier.
Brokers said the rise came on renewed rumours that a third party was interested in buying part of Cable & Wireless' 59 percent stake in the company.
Cathay Pacific shares gained HK$0.15 to HK$11.80 after shrugging off the airline's grounding of its fleet of 11 Airbus A330s due to problems with Rolls Royce Trent 700 engines.
Brokers said the high turnover was partly due to profit-taking in red chips, which accounted for six of the 10 most traded counters on Tuesday.

Chu Kong Shipping, the most traded, retreated from its day high of HK$5.40 to close at HK$4.65, up HK$0.075. Shares of the Chinese shipping company, which carried an initial public offer price of HK$1.20, made their debut last Friday.
Profit-taking hit CITIC Pacific, which lost HK$0.50 to HK$45.00, and Shanghai Industrial, which shed HK$0.80 to HK$45.40.
